description:
FILED s470bo (Opus, 2026-09-05) while fixing #1173 (`5 % 0` answered NaN where
perl dies).  PRE-EXISTING.  #1173 explicitly said "the NaN answers for the
OTHER three conditions were NOT probed here -- measure each against perl
before touching them"; this task IS that measurement, and one of the three is
wrong.

THE ARM (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, `%p-modulo` after s470bo; `%p-%-slow` before it):

    (or (%pcl-nan-p na) (%pcl-nan-p nb)
        (and (floatp na) (sb-ext:float-infinity-p na))
        (and (floatp nb) (sb-ext:float-infinity-p nb)))   ; <- this one
    -> quiet NaN

MEASURED vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s470bo/d2.pl in the s470bo worktree):

    expression      perl            PCL
    5 % inf         5               NaN     <- WRONG
    -5 % inf        Inf             NaN     <- WRONG
    5 % -inf        -Inf            NaN     <- WRONG
    -5 % -inf       -5              NaN     <- WRONG
    inf % 5         NaN             NaN     ok
    -inf % 5        NaN             NaN     ok
    inf % inf       NaN             NaN     ok
    5 % nan         NaN             NaN     ok
    nan % 5         NaN             NaN     ok

So perl's rule is NOT "an infinity anywhere gives NaN".  With an infinite
RIGHT operand perl computes the ordinary mathematical modulo â `a - b*floor(a/b)`,
which carries the SIGN OF THE RIGHT OPERAND, so `5 % inf` is 5 and `-5 % inf`
is Inf.  It is only an infinite or NaN LEFT operand (and a NaN right one) that
gives NaN.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH #1173.  #1173's own text limits itself to the zero
case, and the zero case is a DIE while these are values; the fix here is a
different shape (the float branch has to compute a modulo rather than answer a
constant) and wants its own probe set, including the truncation question â
perl's `%` normally truncates BOTH operands to integers (`5 % 3.7` is 2), and
it plainly cannot truncate an infinity, so the float path is a second rule, not
the same one with a wider guard.

BAR when taken: the nine rows above; the sign rule on both signs of both
operands; `$x %= inf` (the compound twin â it reaches the same `%p-modulo`
after s470bo, where before s470bo it raised a raw CL error); the gate; the full
sweep (a `cl/` change is invisible to corpus-diff) and the op/ companion leg.

=== DONE (s473d) ===
SHIPPED as member 2 of s473d, commit "member 2 (#1191 = #1248(a)): `%` has TWO
regimes and the RIGHT operand picks one -- `5 % Inf` is 5, not NaN".

pp_modulo's two regimes are implemented arm for arm: the UV path (both
operands fit), the NV path (the right operand does not), and the
round-to-nearest promotion between them.  Helpers %pcl-fmod and %pcl-nv;
p-%'s fast path stays FIXNUMS, so the ordinary case is untouched.

BARS: gate 223 files / 7701 rows, xs-only; three probe files, 145 rows,
byte-identical to perl 5.40.3 on both emission paths (default and
PCL_OPT=none); ir-conform rows 251-numeric and 252-numeric left
known-fail.tsv BY EDIT; docs/ir-spec.md section 3.5 is the normative
statement; guard rows in Pl/t/numeric-repr-01.t (B1, B2) inverse-verified on a
c4304834 extraction.  Companion op/ leg on the final tree: op/pow.t 268/0,
op/int.t 19/0, op/sprintf.t 534/25, op/sprintf2.t 1679/25, op/array.t 171/24
-- every file equal to its baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv snapshot, 0 movers.
subject: `5 % Inf` answers NaN where perl answers 5 â %p-%-slow lumps an INFINITE RIGHT operand in with NaN, and only the LEFT one is NaN in perl
